question.text: This son of Henry the Fowler was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 962. He defeated Magyar forces at Lechfeld.
question.clue: Much of his ruling strength came from his namesake system of installing his own bishops, and later in his rule, he deposed John XII in favor of Leo VIII for the papacy.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Luebeck ended the Danish involvement in this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict that began with the Bohemian Revolt and the Defenestration of Prague and primarily pitted the Hapsburgs and their allies against the Bourbons and their allies.
swap.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

question.leadin: Name these things associated with the Crusades.
question.text: This man, known as "red beard" drowned in a river while on the way to fight Saladin.
question.clue: This ruler drowned in the Saleph River during an invasion he undertook with Philip II Augustus.

swap.leadin: A pre-Protestant Christian group named for this man prompted a series of namesake Bohemian wars that lasted from 1419 to 1433.
swap.text: Name this Bohemian priest, who was an advocate of realism in the Catholic Church and was a strong proponent of John Wycliffe, whose writings were first banned by Pope Innocent VII ["the seventh"].
swap.clue: Prokop the Great led forces that pioneered the use of war wagons among this man's Taborite followers in a 15th-century conflict.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Thirty Years' War.
question.text: The Bohemian period of the Thirty Years' War was ended by this 1620 battle near Prague, in which the Count of Tilly defeated Protestant forces lead by Christian of Anhalt.
question.clue: Descartes may have been present at this one-hour battle, as an observer in the army of the count of Bucquoy.

swap.leadin: This group developed special war wagons that provided some of the first mobile artillery in history.
swap.text: Name this group that followed the teachings of a reforming theologian who was burned at the stake after the Council of Constance.
swap.clue: These people, led by Jan Zelivsky, threw Catholic magistrates out of a window during the First Defenestration of Prague.

question.leadin: Events in Eastern Europe sometimes happen in threes.
question.text: Though chronologically the third, the Second event of this name provoked the Thirty Years' War, when two Imperial governors were cast out of a window from the Bohemian Chancellery.
question.clue: The first, in 1419, involved the killing of seven council members by a crowd of Hussites.

swap.leadin: 27 leaders of one revolt named for this historic region were executed in the Old Town Square of its capital.
swap.text: Name this historic region in which Protestants revolted against Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II in 1618. That revolt began after two of the emperor's representatives were defenestrated in this historic region's capital.
swap.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

question.leadin: This man may have helped complete Odo of Metz's designs for a palace in Aachen, and he once dispatched a servant to pilfer holy remains from Rome to increase the piety of churches he founded.
question.text: Identify this colleague of Alcuin, a preeminent Frankish biographer from the eighth and ninth centuries.
question.clue: The preface to this notoriously short man's most famous work was written by Walafrid Strabo.

swap.text: This Hapsburg convened the Diet of Worms (VURMS) and Council of Trent as emperor from 1519 to 1558.
swap.clue: Long before his abdication to a monastery due to his gout, this ruler called Martin Luther to defend his views at the Diet of Worms ("vurms").

question.text: The 983 revolt was faced by the second emperor with this name. Margrave Gero, who campaigned against the Wends, served the first emperor with this name who was crowned by Pope John XII in 962.
question.answerHtml: Otto [accept Otto II or Otto I; accept Otto the Great]
question.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

swap.text: The precise makeup of the seven electors was set down in this 1356 decree, sponsored by Emperor Charles IV.
swap.clue: This 1356 decree that outlined the system of electing the Holy Roman Emperor.

question.text: The Falun mine was initially outpaced by production at the mines at Rammelsberg. Those mines were first discovered during the reign of this ruler, and were described in the chronicle of his advisor Widukind of Corvey.
question.answerHtml: Otto the Great [or Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor; or Otto der Grosse; prompt on Otto]
question.clue: He subjugated Berengar of Ivrea to rescue the kidnapped Adelaide, whom he married, making him King of Lombardy.

swap.leadin: This group was led by Philip the Magnanimous of Hesse and John Frederick of Saxony.
swap.text: Name this alliance of Lutheran princes, mostly located within northern Germany. It eventually fought a namesake war with the Holy Roman Empire and Charles V in the 1540's.
swap.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

question.leadin: One commander in this battle placed the Saxon forces of Johann Georg on his left flank and decided not use the immobile "tercio" formation.
question.text: Name this 1631 battle of the Thirty Years War, a decisive victory for the Protestants.
question.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.

swap.leadin: This emperor besieged Viterbo to restore a loyal imperial garrison, only to see papal representative Ranieri Capocci ("ron-YAIR-ee ka-PO-chee") massacre the loyalists after he signed a peace treaty.
swap.text: Name this emperor who promulgated the Constitutions of Melfi in his Kingdom of Sicily. This husband of Yolande of Jerusalem launched the Sixth Crusade to recapture the holy city.
swap.clue: This 13th-century king, called Stupor Mundi or "the astonishment of the world," drew on an Arabic text by Moamin to write "On the Art of Hunting With Birds" in his Sicilian court.

question.text: When the undefeated John Zizka was replaced by Procopius the Great as leader of the Taborite army, emperor Sigismund and the utraquists teamed up to smack him down in this 1434 battle also known as Cesky Brod.
question.clue: The Taborites were eventually defeated by an Utraquist coalition at this battle, after which they made peace with the Council of Basel via the Compact of Iglau.

swap.text: This one-eyed general revolutionized mobile warfare by mounting cannons on armored wagons and led the Taborites to a series of victories over the Bohemian Crusade. After his 1424 death, Taborite leadership passed to Procop the Great.
swap.clue: This one-eyed Taborite general, a reformist commander in the Hussite Wars, withstood Sigismund's siege of Prague at the Battle of Vitkov Hill. His tactics included arming wagon circles with cannons.

question.leadin: He spent the first few years of his reign putting down a revolt led by Boleslav of Bohemia and Henry the Wrangler. FTPE.
question.text: Name this emperor, whose brothers included the rebellious Liudolf of Swabia.

swap.text: Frederick Barbarossa withdrew his support of Antipope Callixtus III after this 1176 battle, in which he was decisively defeated by Alberto da Guissano and the forces of the Lombard League.
swap.clue: The carroccio, an oxen-drawn war wagon topped with a sacred altar, was used at this 1176 battle, which prompted its loser to sign the Treaty of Venice.
